label: def:qns-unit-layers
title: Unit layers of the $q$-NS classical limit: substrate (vanishing $\nu_q$) and physical ($c_q$-rescaled, $\nu_{\mathrm{phys}} = 1/(2q)$)
html:
The classical limit q \to 1^+ of the internal q-Navier–Stokes dynamics may be taken in two unit systems, which differ by the canonical substrate scale c_q = 1/(q-1). Every statement about the classical limit of a q-fluid quantity carries exactly one of the two layer tags below.

Substrate layer. Coordinates (x, t) as carried by the substrate: wavenumbers are the q-integers [n]_q, and the viscosity is the derived ladder quantity

  \nu_q \;=\; \frac{q-1}{2q},

which vanishes as q \to 1^+. In this layer the classical limit is a vanishing-viscosity (Euler-type) limit.

Physical layer. Coordinates (X, T) = (c_q\,x,\; c_q\,t) with velocity unrescaled — a rescaling by an existing derived scale, introducing no new degree of freedom. Under this map k_{\mathrm{phys}} = (q-1)\,k_{\mathrm{sub}} (the ladder becomes a continuum grid of spacing q-1), enstrophies convert by (q-1)^2, and the viscosity becomes

  \nu_{\mathrm{phys}} \;=\; c_q\,\nu_q \;=\; \frac{1}{2q},

exactly — an algebraic identity, with \tfrac12 - \nu_{\mathrm{phys}} \leq (q-1)/2. In this layer the classical limit is a fixed-viscosity Navier–Stokes limit, the setting of the Clay formulation.

Never straddle the layers (strict). A single computed quantity, estimate, or claim must not mix substrate-layer and physical-layer inputs; every fluid-dynamics statement about the classical limit names its layer, and cross-layer comparisons go through the conversion identities above. The two layers can give different answers to the same-sounding question: the spectral pile-up question of the uniformity reduction is answered negatively in the substrate layer (tail enstrophy above a fixed band grows without bound as q \to 1^+, the receding dissipation range filling in) and affirmatively in the physical layer (the converted tail vanishes), per the witness qns-tail-pileup-probe.witness.json.
